quotes.text: Review fraud patterns and their impact on your business in the Dashboard.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: By default, statistics reflect the prior 30 days of transaction history, following a 24-hour delay.
Users with access to [Sigma](https://stripe.com/sigma) can further analyze their data by using the **View in Sigma** link

findings: New 5–14 retains Dashboard fraud-analysis purpose and identifies the same two query-selected views as old 19–21 and 159–161: Radar Analytics center (radar-dash=rac) and Legacy Radar overview (radar-dash=legacy). Diff 7–301 replaces their embedded text with a selector. November establishes no new Dashboard prerequisite, feature state or product removal. Old default Analytics Center and New overview toggle at 17 remain May-dated.

May describes the newer Dashboard Overview as gauges of merchant fraud, Radar interventions, peers and monitoring, with 30-day prior history and 24-hour delay, configurable transaction amount vs count, arrival vs payment date, deduplicating per PaymentIntent and optional SetupIntents. The panels separately show Fraud (fraud disputes and early fraud warnings not escalated), all-type Disputes (disputed divided by successful payments) and Blocks (high-risk versus own rules; blocked divided by successful in this view's prose). Worst-case line is modeled, may not show at low volume or if fraud-arrival-date option enabled, and delayed disputes can change rates (old 23–102). Preserve formulas view-specifically. Legacy old 205–226 uses blocked divided by attempted instead. The source line 25's 'disabled' should document the toggle may be absent under either stated condition, not an account/lifetime change.

May Rule matches reports actions actually taken on screened transactions. It distinguishes Transactions rate/count/volume and Blocked top rules, 3DS authentication outcomes, Allow outcome categories including fraud disputes or early fraud warnings, and manual Review state transitions. In old 148–153, disputed supersedes previously in-review/approved once filed. Source 27 compresses the Allow branch to disputed and refunded, leaving out un-escalated early fraud warnings in the grouped fraud outcome (old 135–141). This action panel is distinct from the all-disputes panel and late projections.

May legacy documents 3DS challenge→screened→disputed flow, regional vs similar business benchmarks, estimated false positives, benchmark cohort privacy and opt-out. Similar-business benchmarks require many dozens per cohort, only businesses with significant payments included, equal per-entity votes. A business can opt out of contributing while continuing to view benchmarks (old 163–199). Source 45 needs qualification of '≥dozens' and feedback path/privacy, rather than implying a precise general minimum. Legacy attempted payments include supported screened retries; local discussion says Terminal/card-present and recurring Stripe Billing payments aren't screened, and SetupIntents are screened but excluded from these counts. The newer chart setting optionally includes SetupIntents; neither point establishes a November-wide product policy (old 41–48,200–232).

May legacy distinguishes fraudulent dispute cohort by payment creation from disputes received by dispute creation, plotting observed versus historically projected possible maximum for recent 120-day cohorts, excluding inquiries unless escalated in disputes section. Radar for Fraud Teams manual reviews shows queue statuses; disputed in-review payments automatically close the review (old 235–275). Daily UTC computation, 24-hour access, six-month legacy default, default-currency aggregation based on daily FX and CSV download are documented. View in Sigma is for users with Sigma access and opens the generating SQL. Source 44 and concept 144 omit that prerequisite (old 277–293).

May Analytics compares fraud/dispute rates with card-network monitoring thresholds and reports current status/possible penalties, with program-specific detail at old 295–299. The heading occurs at the end following the legacy section, without requiring a claim that the route is exclusive to the newer view (source 29). Monitoring status, estimates, fraud warnings and disputes are distinct measurements rather than a guaranteed fraud, enforcement, or payment outcome. Old 8–15 routes to Fraud Insights, Sigma and Data Pipeline as complementary analysis.

May newer Blocks formula uses successful payments while legacy rate uses attempted payments (old 94 vs 205–226). May new chart's optional SetupIntent inclusion at 48 is distinct from legacy attempted-page exclusion of screened SetupIntents at 220. Read metric by view and retain separate payment-arrival/creation date contexts.

unresolved_questions: November child views were not read. Current account dashboard defaults, feature entitlement, active metric calculations, export availability and network assessment do not follow from the selector.

source_assessments.reason: November is navigation only. Independently qualify Sigma access and benchmark visibility, restore important view-specific metric boundaries, and preserve the May date.

answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/radar/analytics establishes Dashboard fraud analytics navigation to Radar Analytics center and Legacy Radar overview (new raw lines 5-14). It does not freshly describe metric behavior. The May 10 guide describes the newer view as default, with 30 days of history after a 24-hour delay, selection of count or volume, fraud-arrival or payment date, retry deduplication and optional SetupIntents. Fraud, all disputes and blocks are distinct charts. The newer Blocks ratio uses successful payments, while legacy block rate uses attempted payments. Modeled worst-case fraud is conditional and distinct from observed rates (old raw lines 17-48 and 62-102, old raw lines 200-232). Rule actions and review outcomes are separate reporting, while legacy covers the 3DS/screening/dispute flow, privacy-gated benchmark cohorts, six-month default, exports and daily updates (old raw lines 104-199 and 235-299). source-stripe-radar-analytics.md captures the core views but needs the Sigma access prerequisite, benchmark limits and action/metric distinctions. These are reporting states rather than payment or monitoring program outcomes for a particular account.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/analytics, the November 7, 2026 difference is presentation and navigation: the full May 10 guide had embedded Radar Analytics center and legacy views, and November links the same query routes (new raw lines 9-14, old raw lines 17-23 and 159-165). Neither a product behavior change nor removal of May functionality is evidenced. Preserve the dated 30-day and six-month defaults, 24-hour lag, version-scoped SetupIntent and screened-payment treatment, denominator differences, conditional estimate visibility, similar-business cohort qualifications and continued viewing after opting out, and Sigma permission separate from CSV (old raw lines 30-48 and 62-95, old raw lines 189-232 and 277-299). Correct source-stripe-radar-analytics.md on the baseline qualifiers without treating them as November changes. Keep both dated raw routes and the existing reciprocal Stripe Radar concept and source links, through the root/provider indexes, and retain the separate dispute measurement and card monitoring routes.
